9.12.1. qnav.waypoints.generation

9.12.1.1. generation.py

summary:

Handles all interpolation and generation of waypoint trajectory data. This module contains a collection of functions for generating waypoint trajectories for various vehicle models. In addition to this, waypoint data can be imported from CSV files or binary numpy files.

authors:
Prof. Jason Ralph - jfralph@liverpool.ac.uk
Michael Wright - mjwright@liverpool.ac.uk
version:

1.1.0 - Includes fixes and improvements.

qnav.waypoints.generation.get_positions(lat_points: ndarray, lon_points: ndarray, alt_points: ndarray, vehicle_model: Vehicle, frequency: float = 200.0, avg_speed: float = 100.0, travel_times: ndarray = None)[source]

This function interpolates positions (latitude, longitude and altitude) between provided waypoints that are separated by either stated distance or time (not both). The generated route is subject to the limitations of the vehicle. The produced route can then be used for calculating the required trajectory for simulations.

Parameters:

  • lat_points (numpy.ndarray) – The decimal latitude points for the given waypoints. Use negative values for southern coordinates (in degrees).

  • lon_points (numpy.ndarray) – The decimal longitude points for the given waypoints. Use negative values for western coordinates (in degrees).

  • alt_points (numpy.ndarray) – The altitude for the given waypoints (in metres).

  • vehicle_model (Vehicle) – An initialised vehicle model containing the manoeuvring limitations to consider when generating the waypoint positions.

  • frequency (float) – The simulation’s update frequency. This is used for calculating the number of intermediate points and total number of waypoints to return.

  • avg_speed (float) – The average vehicle speed for the given waypoints. This is used to calculate the travel times between waypoints. This value is replaced by ‘travel_times’. Therefore, a value for this is not required if the travel times are known.

  • travel_times (numpy.ndarray) – The time (in seconds) when each waypoint is reached. This is required for interpolating the position between points.

Returns:

An array containing column for latitude, longitude and altitude of the vehicle at each time step.

Return type:

numpy.ndarray (n-by-4 elements)

qnav.waypoints.generation.interpolate_positions(base_points: ndarray, frequency: float) → ndarray[source]

Interpolates the base waypoints at the new higher frequency. This function can be used to speed up and stabilise the calculation of the waypoint positions, by interpolating the intermediate steps.

Parameters:

  • base_points (np.ndarray) – The base waypoint data to interpolate.

  • frequency (float) – The frequency to interpolate the waypoint data by.

Returns:

The interpolated version of the given waypoint positions.

Return type:

np.ndarray

qnav.waypoints.generation.produce_noise(num_rows: int, first_val: float, noise_val: float, dt_vdp: float)[source]

This function generated random noise that can be added to various aspects. For instance, this function can be used to produce noise for position, attitude and oscillation displacement. This function is required so that the noise generated is done so in a self-balancing manner such that the displacements do not cause permanent or increasing drift.

Parameters:

  • num_rows (int) – The number of noise values to produce.

  • first_val (float or numpy.array) – The first generated noise value(s).

  • noise_val (float) – The scale of the noise values.

  • dt_vdp – The dampening factor to apply. This is used to prevent the noise from causing permanent or excessive drift.

Returns:

The generated noise subject to the given parameters.

Return type:

numpy.array

qnav.waypoints.generation.moving_average(input_array, window_size: int = 5)[source]

Obtains the “sliding window average” for values of an array. This function calculates the moving average of a given 1D array using the same approach as MATLAB. A sliding window is passed over the given array. For the centre (right) element the moving average is calculated using the values covered by the window. This means that fewer elements are covered at the start and end of the array. The returned values are the same size as the given array.

Parameters:

  • input_array (NumPy array) – The values which the moving average is going to be calculated for. This must be a 1D array.

  • window_size (int) – The size of the sliding window. Must be an integer.

Returns:

The calculated moving averages for the given array.

Return type:

NumPy array

qnav.waypoints.generation.rescale_values(values)[source]

A simple function that allows angles to be re-scaled to prevent inaccuracy calculations between angles differences.

Parameters:

values (numpy.array) – The angle values to be rescaled.

Returns:

The given values re-scaled between -pi/2 and pi/2.

Return type:

numpy.array

qnav.waypoints.generation.get_simple_trajectory_values(waypoints: ndarray, gravity_model: GravityModel, given_attitudes: ndarray = None, attitude_times: ndarray = None, smoothing_window_time: float = None, smoothing_passes: int = None, step_size: int = 2, virtual_mem_file: Path = None)[source]

Calculates the trajectory information and properties from given waypoints. This function calculates the trajectory properties for each position for a given set of waypoints. Only simple properties are generated, without any added noise, vibrations or oscillations of the platform. In previous releases this function was refereed to as legacy waypoint generation.

Parameters:

  • waypoints (NumPy Matrix (n-by-4 elements)) – The interpolated waypoint array previously generated. It is important any changes/updates to the waypoints (such as altitude changes) are applied to the waypoints before using this function.

  • gravity_model (GravityModel) – The gravity model used to calculate local gravity. This is required for calculating the downwards gravitation acceleration and its impact on the platform for each axis.

  • given_attitudes (numpy.array (n-elements)) – (Optional) The requested attitude of the vehicle at given times. Intermediate attitude values will be interpolated.

  • attitude_times (numpy.array (n-elements)) – (Optional) The requested corresponding times for the given attitudes. These timestamps are used to interpolate intermediate attitude values.

  • smoothing_window_time (float) – (Optional) The size of the smoothing (moving average) window to use for smoothing the calculated waypoint velocities. This is useful for removing noise.

  • smoothing_passes (int) – (Optional) The number of smoothing passes (iterations) to perform on the calculated waypoint velocities.

  • step_size (int) – (Optional) The step size used for calculating the velocity between upcoming waypoints (default=1).

  • virtual_mem_file (bool) – The on-disk file to use for virtual memory. Will be created or overwritten

Returns:

A matrix containing the position, velocity, acceleration, attitude, angle rates and gravitational acceleration (and gradient) for each time step.

Return type:

NumPy Matrix (n-by-16 elements)

qnav.waypoints.generation.get_trajectory_values(waypoints: ndarray, gravity_model: GravityModel, vehicle_model: Vehicle, given_attitudes: ndarray = None, attitude_times: ndarray = None, smoothing_window_time: float = None, smoothing_passes: int = None, step_size: int = 2, virtual_mem_file: Path = None)[source]

Using waypoints route information generated prior, this function will calculate the velocity, acceleration, attitude, angle rates and gravitational acceleration (and gradient) for each time step. This function calculates said values in an efficient vectorised manner while ensuring they abide by the given vehicle model’s limitations.

Parameters:

  • waypoints (NumPy Matrix (n-by-4 elements)) – The interpolated waypoint array previously generated. It is important any changes/updates to the waypoints (such as altitude changes) are applied to the waypoints before using this function.

  • gravity_model (GravityModel) – The gravity model used to calculate local gravity. This is required for calculating the downwards gravitation acceleration and its impact on the platform for each axis.

  • vehicle_model (Vehicle) – An initialised vehicle model containing the manoeuvring limitations to consider when generating the waypoint positions.

  • given_attitudes (numpy.array (n-elements)) – (Optional) The requested attitude of the vehicle at given times. Intermediate attitude values will be interpolated.

  • attitude_times (numpy.array (n-elements)) – (Optional) The requested corresponding times for the given attitudes. These timestamps are used to interpolate intermediate attitude values.

  • smoothing_window_time (float) – (Optional) The size of the smoothing (moving average) window to use for smoothing the calculated waypoint velocities. This is useful for removing noise.

  • smoothing_passes (int) – (Optional) The number of smoothing passes (iterations) to perform on the calculated waypoint velocities.

  • step_size (int) – (Optional) The step size used for calculating the velocity between upcoming waypoints (default=1).

  • virtual_mem_file (bool) – The on-disk file to use for virtual memory. Will be created or overwritten

Returns:

A matrix containing the position, velocity, acceleration, attitude, angle rates and gravitational acceleration (and gradient) for each time step.

Return type:

NumPy Matrix (n-by-16 elements)

qnav.waypoints.generation.load_waypoint_csv(filepath: Path, down_sample_rate: int = 1)[source]

This function will extract the values from a given trajectory file, formatted as comma-separated-values. Once the relevant information is extracted, 7 rows will be returned containing information of the extracted timestamps, latitude points, longitude points, altitude points and three attitude angles. These rows are returned within a list.

Parameters:

  • filepath (str or Path) – The location of the CSV trajectory file to read.

  • down_sample_rate (int) – The down sampling multiplier to apply. This can be used to skip rows for cases where CSV waypoints are given too frequently or spaced too closely together.

Returns:

A list containing 7 arrays holding the extracted timestamps, latitude points, longitude points, altitude points and attitude angles from the given CSV trajectory file.

Return type:

NumPy array

qnav.waypoints.generation.crop_waypoints(waypoints: ndarray, max_time: float)[source]

  • max_time (float) – The maximum time for the return waypoint data.

Returns:

The cropped waypoint data

Return type:

qnav.waypoints.generation.save_waypoints(waypoints: ndarray, file_path: Path, allow_overwrite: bool = False)[source]

Returns:

The loaded waypoint data.

Return type:

numpy.array (n-by-16 elements)

qnav.waypoints.generation.read_csv_waypoints(file_path: Path, delimiter: str = ',') → dict[str, ndarray | None][source]

Reads given CSV waypoint file and returns the records contained within it. For a given file path, attempts to read its content and return it’s extracted records inside a dictionary.

Parameters:

  • file_path (Path) – The CSV file to attempt to read waypoint data from.

  • delimiter (str) – The delimiter used to represent column breaks. By default, this is a comma, but other characters can be used.

Returns:

A dictionary holding the extracted data.

Return type:

dict[str, np.ndarray | None]
